To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The prevalence of hypertension is increasing worldwide and is expected to continue to rise in the coming decades; 2) The prevalence of uncontrolled blood pressure is high, even among treated hypertensive individuals; and 3) The prevalence of resistant hypertension is increasing and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality.

the relationship of hypertension-associated events and medication, compliance and adherence in hypertensive patients after starting antihypertensive therapy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a single antihypertensive medication is the best strategy to initiate treatment of hypertension, and the most effective and cost-effective strategy to treat hypertension is the use of two or more antihypertensives in combination.
the use of a single antihypertensive medication, whether a beta-blocker, an ACE inhibitor, or an ARB, in the treatment of hypertension is safe and efficacious.
the use of antihypertensive medications in hypertensive patients, especially in those with a history of cardiovascular events, is beneficial and should be continued as long as it is tolerated.

we have developed a new method for the detection of the first hypertension-related event in a cohort of patients treated with antihypertensive drugs, and we have shown that the first event is related to the type of medication, adherence and persistence.

the results indicate that the first event of hypertension (HTN) is related to medication, compliance, persistence and adherence to therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

patients who experience the first hypertension-associated clinical event (HTA) while being treated with a monotherapy are more likely to be compliant with their medication and to persist in their therapy, compared with patients who remain free of HTA.
